analysis: The supplied change is documentation only. CHANGELOG.md gains one line under 'Unreleased — provider 0.9.17' (patch around line 63). It says an explicitly configured TMPDIR is honored for anonymous runtime metallib snapshots, with unlink-before-copy and digest binding preserved, and that an invalid or unwritable directory fails without falling back. The changelog edit itself adds no code, configuration or attack surface, and it does not change any assumption in the threat model. The four units (metadata, patch, two base-text chunks) were examined. The base-text chunks contain only pre-existing changelog prose and none of it is altered. The described behavior would be a provider-side change (TB-003 operator vs process, T-013/T-014/T-050 temp-file exposure, and the provider binary hash and qualification path under T-034/T-054). The corresponding provider source is not in this batch, so I could not check whether an operator-controlled TMPDIR weakens the metallib integrity binding or leaks data into a world-readable location. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. A later pass should review the Swift provider diff if one exists, looking at the digest check, the unlink-before-copy ordering, file permissions, and the fail-closed behavior on invalid TMPDIR. This changelog-only PR has no cross-file interactions.
